title: Incident bot: prompt for + pin related SUP Jira tickets in incident bridges
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Support Escalation Playbook Refresh / Known-Issues Sprint (2026-02)
dependencies: INT-332 (Jira): Update Slack automation for support bridges
INT-333 (Jira): Jira automation for SLA reminders + required fields
Support playbook: Slack bridge and incident channel conventions (Confluence)
links: Slack thread (eng-oncall): standardize required context + pinned template (#eng-oncall, 1772003901)
Slack thread (incidents): partial eu-west degradation bridge referencing SUP-1850 (#incidents, 1772008012)
Email: Incident bridge template + Jira linking (Rafael Mendes, 2026-02-10)
Related SUP examples: SUP-1842, SUP-1850, SUP-1860
content:
Context / problem
- During customer-impacting incidents, Support often opens/links one or more SUP Jira tickets (customer escalations, comms tracking, SLA timers).
- We consistently lose discoverability after bridge channels quiet down: SUP links get dropped in scrollback, pinned items vary by channel owner, and incident summaries lack the canonical ticket list.
- Result: slower follow-ups (credits requests, postmortem customer threads, repeated triage questions), and Support has to re-assemble context from scattered Slack messages.

Goal
Improve the incident-bot workflow so that every incident bridge channel has a durable, discoverable set of related SUP ticket links, and the incident summary includes them.

Non-goals
- Replacing Jira automation (required fields / SLA timers) handled in INT-333.
- Changing the incident severity policy or Support SLA policy.
- Auto-creating SUP tickets (Support owns ticket creation; bot should only collect/link).

Proposed behavior (Slack)
1) When an incident bridge is created (or when bot posts the initial bridge message), bot prompts channel for:
   - Primary SUP ticket (required if customer impact is confirmed)
   - Additional related SUP tickets (optional)
   - A short customer impact summary (1–2 lines; customer-safe)
2) Bot validates formatting:
   - Accept SUP-#### keys (preferred)
   - Accept full Jira URL; bot normalizes to key
   - Reject/reprompt if key is malformed
3) Bot posts a canonical message in the bridge channel:
   - "Related Support tickets:" with bullet list of SUP keys as links
   - "Owner:" (Support on-call / incident comms owner) if provided
   - "Last updated:" timestamp
4) Bot pins the canonical message automatically.
   - If pin fails due to permissions, bot posts a fallback message tagging #eng-oncall and instructs a human to pin.
5) Bot keeps the pinned canonical message updated when new SUP tickets are added (edit message rather than spamming new posts).

Proposed behavior (incident summary)
- Incident bot summary payload (whatever is posted to #incidents / stored in incident record) includes:
  - sup_tickets: comma-separated list (e.g., SUP-1850, SUP-1860)
  - sup_primary: single key (if designated)
  - links: clickable Jira URLs

Edge cases / rules
- If incident is internal-only (no customer impact): SUP tickets optional; bot should allow skipping with "no customer ticket" response.
- If incident spans multiple customers: allow multiple SUP tickets; designate one as primary if possible.
- If Support opens a SUP after the incident starts: allow adding later via a simple slash command (e.g., /incident add-sup SUP-####).
- If a bridge is created from #support (not yet moved to #incidents): still capture SUP links; when bridge later becomes an incident, the links carry over.

Implementation notes
- Permissions: ensure bot has "pins" scope in bridge channels; confirm with Slack app config.
- Jira linking: Jira base URL should be environment-configured; do not hardcode.
- Storage: if incident-bot persists incident metadata, add field for sup_ticket_keys (string list) and sup_primary_key.
- UX: keep prompts short; default to a single prompt with examples, then accept multiple replies.

Acceptance criteria
- For a new incident bridge channel, within 2 minutes of creation, there is a pinned message listing related SUP ticket(s) OR a clear failure message instructing manual pin with the exact content to pin.
- Adding a SUP ticket after creation updates the pinned canonical message (no duplicate canonical posts).
- Incident summary output includes the same SUP list.
- Works for at least these real-world flows:
  - Streaming disconnect escalation where Support created SUP-1842 before incident
  - Regional degradation where Support created SUP-1850 after incident started
  - Credits request / exec escalation follow-up tied to SUP-1860

Testing plan
- Unit: parse/normalize SUP keys from text and URLs; ensure de-dupe.
- Integration: Slack pin/edit message flows; validate behavior when pin permission is missing.
- Manual: dry run in #incidents-sandbox with mock SUP keys.

Rollout
- Stage to sandbox first.
- Announce in #support and #eng-oncall once shipped; include "how to add SUP" command.
- After 1 week, check:
  - % incidents with at least one linked SUP
  - # follow-up pings from Support asking for the incident channel / context

Security / sensitivity
- Do not pull any ticket description text into Slack automatically (avoid customer-sensitive content leakage).
- Only post SUP keys + links; impact summary must be customer-safe.

Work items
- Add slash command: /incident add-sup SUP-#### (and optional multiple keys)
- Add initial prompt + canonical message
- Implement pin/edit behavior
- Include SUP list in incident summary record
- Docs: update Support bridge conventions to reference the bot behavior

Progress / updates
2026-02-12 (Rafael Mendes)
- Confirmed with Support (Owen Phillips) that the main ask is durable SUP discoverability in bridge channels; scrolling back is the current failure mode.
- Agreed we should not auto-create SUP tickets; Support still owns creation and SLA timers.

2026-02-14 (Benji Okafor)
- Implemented parsing + normalization (SUP key + Jira URL).
- Added incident metadata fields: sup_ticket_keys, sup_primary_key.
- Next: Slack pin behavior + edit-in-place.

2026-02-18 (Benji Okafor)
- Pin/edit flow working in sandbox; discovered bot lacks pin permission in newly-created channels depending on who creates channel.
- Action: coordinate with Dylan Brooks to confirm Slack app scopes + channel creation workflow; may need to ensure bot is channel creator or invited with correct role.

Open questions
- Should we also support non-SUP keys (e.g., internal INT-### or ENG-###) in the pinned message? (Proposal: allow, but keep default prompt focused on SUP.)
- Where should the incident summary be posted (existing #incidents bot summary vs internal incident record only)? Need confirmation from SRE.

Owner(s)
- Eng: Benji Okafor
- SRE reviewer: Rafael Mendes
- Support stakeholders: Owen Phillips / Dev Patel
- Tooling/Jira automation: Dylan Brooks (FYI)
comments: Rafael Mendes (2026-02-10): This is one of the top paper-cuts from the playbook refresh. We need SUP links pinned so support escalations survive beyond bridge scrollback. Please align with the bridge template email thread and keep content customer-safe (keys + links only).
Dev Patel (2026-02-11): +1. The bridge template is ready; missing piece is consistency. Biggest win: pin a single canonical message and update it, rather than 10 people pasting links.

Dylan Brooks (2026-02-18): Slack app pin permission is inconsistent across channels created by workflows vs humans. Let’s confirm current app scopes and whether our channel creation flow can ensure the bot is added with permission before it tries to pin.
